Pochayiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Pochayiv's Jewish community, present from the 17th century, largely made its living from trade with Orthodox Christian pilgrims visiting the town's major monastery. The local Hevra Kadisha performed a distinctive service: helping Jewish converts reconvert to Judaism and sending them into the Austrian Empire for safety. The Karlin-Stolin Hasidic dynasty predominated in Pochayiv, and rabbis Haim Roinick and his son Jacob-Yosef (1862–1910) served the community at the turn of the 20th century. In 1919, the Polish army organized a massacre of the town's Jews. During the Holocaust, the ghetto's liquidation in September 1942 saw 794 people murdered, about 500 of them shot directly at this cemetery. Gravestones from this site were later used to rebuild a former synagogue into a school; the cemetery itself was demolished in the 1960s, according to local residents.
